subject: brown rat
title: Rats Were Filmed Snatching Flying Bats Out of the Air in the Dark

scenes.text: Rats were filmed catching bats in mid-air. In the dark.
In Bad Segeberg, Germany, 30,000 bats pour into one cave to hibernate.
Infrared cameras caught brown rats waiting for them, upright on their hind legs.
As a bat flew past, a rat grabbed it with its front paws and killed it with a bite.
Rats see poorly. Scientists suspect their whiskers feel the wingbeats.
Thirteen kills on camera, 52 carcasses in the cave. Fifteen rats could eat 2,100 bats a winter.

description:
Brown rats have been filmed plucking flying bats out of the air in the dark, a first for science.
At a hibernation cave in Bad Segeberg, northern Germany, used by more than 30,000 Daubenton's and Natterer's bats, infrared and thermal cameras recorded rats standing upright, balancing on their tails and intercepting bats with their forelegs: 30 attempts and 13 confirmed kills, plus a cache of at least 52 carcasses. The team, led by Florian Gloza-Rausch of Berlin's natural history museum, estimates a colony of 15 rats could eat about 2,100 bats in a winter, roughly 7 percent of the roost. How the rats find bats in the dark is not settled; whiskers and air currents are the suspects. The study appeared in Global Ecology and Conservation in 2025.
Did you think a rat could do that? Comment below.
first_comment: Other rats skipped the acrobatics and crept up on bats that had landed. Did you think a rat could do that?
